entities.name: Philomelos of Phocis
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Philomelus of Phocis was a general in the Third Sacred War (343-339 BCE), leading his forces to victory against the Delians. His actions were motivated by a desire for independence and self-determination, reflecting the complex dynamics between city-states in ancient Greece.

As a member of the Theban aristocracy, Philomelus was part of a broader struggle for power and influence within the region. His brother Onomarchus would later succeed him as general, solidifying their family's legacy in the city-state of Thebes.

The impact of Philomelus' actions can be seen in the subsequent history of the region, where the Delian War led to a significant shift in the balance of power between Athens and Thebes. This, in turn, contributed to the eventual rise of Philip II of Macedon, who would go on to unify the city-states under his rule.

In the world of ancient Greek literature, Philomelus' legacy has been immortalized in the works of the historian Polybius, who wrote extensively about the Third Sacred War and its key figures. This enduring recognition underscores the lasting impact of Philomelus' actions on the course of Greek history.
